append_rules.inline_arm: inline count <= 7: store at inline_array_pointer[inline count], then inline count += 1
append_rules.overflow_arm: inline count > 7: if overflow end == overflow capacity, call grow helper 0x4fc75e0 with (overflow vector address at collection +0x50, overflow end, stack pointer); then store at the old overflow end and advance overflow end by 8

callers.notes: 0x50ec19c is the flush driver mapped by PR #1892 (its phase A call, collection at driver frame -0x1d0). The other two enclosing functions are census only; their call arguments are not pinned here.

collection_layout.count_meaning: inline element count, 0..8 in a consistent collection
collection_layout.element_access: index < 8 reads inline_array_pointer[index]; index >= 8 reads overflow_begin[index - 8] (the bytes compute overflow_begin - 0x40 + index * 8)

frame.canary: fs:0x28 at rsp+0x08, checked on every return path and before the log tail-call

gate_order.name: empty collection
gate_order.rule: total elements == 0 returns immediately, before the flag is read

gate_order.name: lookup
gate_order.rule: call 0x4fec940 with (object at [db +0x68] +0x40, static object at 0x57887a0); a null result returns immediately

gate_order.name: chain guard
gate_order.rule: the lookup result's +0x8e8 field dereferenced, then its +0xc18 field dereferenced; a null at either step returns immediately. The dereferenced value is not otherwise used by this window

gate_order.name: already present
gate_order.rule: if any collection element pointer equals the lookup result, return immediately (no append, no log)

gate_order.name: smallest-key rule
gate_order.rule: walk the list headed at [[db +0x68] +0x40] +0x110 (nodes linked by +0x938, sentinel is the head address); for each node, first compare the node pointer with the lookup result pointer and skip the node when they are identical; otherwise, if the node's +0x948 field is less than or equal to the lookup result's +0x948 field (unsigned cmovae after cmp target,node), return immediately. An empty list passes. Equivalently, append only when the lookup result's +0x948 is strictly smaller than every other list node's +0x948

gate_order.name: append and log
gate_order.rule: append the lookup result to the collection (see append_rules), then tail-call the log callee 0x522ea30 with (level 1, db +0x360, message, file)

grow_call.internals: not pinned by this work item

inferences: The +0x948 field is read as an unsigned ordering key; its source-level name (sequence, version, or deadline) is not pinned.
The db +0x360 argument to the log call is read as a name string for the %s slot; its exact object type is not pinned.
The .bss object at 0x57887a0 is the lookup key; its runtime content is not pinned.

log_record.message: [%s:1980] Force flushing stats CF with automated flush to avoid holding old logs

lookup_call.internals: not pinned by this work item
lookup_call.key_argument: static object at 0x57887a0 (in .bss, runtime-initialised; content not pinned)

observations: The window never writes the db struct except through the callees; its only direct effects are the collection append and the log call.
The empty-collection return precedes the flag check, so an empty collection logs nothing even when the phase flag is set.
The chain guard dereferences two pointers but discards the final value; it is a validity gate, not a value load.
unknowns: Types of the db struct, the +0x68 object, the +0x40 object, the lookup result, and the list nodes.
Source-level meaning of the +0x948 ordering key and of the db +0x4c9 flag.
Call arguments of the two non-driver callers (0x50ecc3e, 0x50ed5a0).

window.name: WAL flush phase A: append the looked-up object to the flush collection
window.returns: void; the collection and one level-1 log record are the observable effects
